title: Combined TECAR/EMS Therapy vs. Standard Manual Therapy for Endometriosis Pelvic Pain
official: Comparative Effects of Combined TECAR Radiofrequency and Electrical Muscle Stimulation Therapy Versus Standard Manual Therapy for Pelvic Pain in Women With Endometriosis
summary: This study compares two ways of delivering a combined radiofrequency (RET), muscle stimulation (Hi-EMS), and pulsed radiofrequency (Hi-TENS) therapy, hands-on by a physical therapist or hands-free using adhesive pads, and compares the combined therapy to hands-on manual therapy alone for pelvic pain in women with endometriosis. Participants attend 8 sessions over 6 weeks.

interventions.name: Hands-on manual pelvic floor physical therapy

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Women age 18 or older with a diagnosis of endometriosis (surgical/histologic or imaging-based)
* Pelvic pain attributable to endometriosis
* Able to attend the 8-session outpatient schedule
* Able to provide written informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Clinical concern for or diagnosis of May-Thurner syndrome with associated risk of deep vein thrombosis (DVT)
* Presence of a cardiac pacemaker, implantable cardioverter-defibrillator, or other active implanted electronic device
* Active or suspected deep vein thrombosis or other uncontrolled clotting disorder
* Open wound, active infection, or compromised skin integrity at planned electrode sites (suprapubic/lower abdominal region and sacral/gluteal region)
* Known malignancy in the region to be treated
* Current pregnancy
* Inability to tolerate electrical stimulation per participant report during device calibration
